question.text: By how many points will Kiko Llaneras beat the Community Prediction in the 2026 Fall Metaculus Cup?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the difference between the Total Score of Kiko Llaneras (username kikollan) and the Community Prediction in the tournament [leaderboard](https://www.metaculus.com/tournament/metaculus-cup-fall-2026/#leaderboard), at the conclusion of the Metaculus Cup Fall 2026.
question.fine_print:
If the Community Prediction has a higher total score than Kiko Llaneras, then this question will resolve to a negative integer.

This question will resolve after all other Metaculus Cup Fall 2026 questions have resolved other than [How many bots will finish in the top 10 of the Metaculus Cup Fall 2026?](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/45619/how-many-bots-will-finish-in-the-top-10-of-the-metaculus-cup-fall-2026/), which will resolve after this one. 

This question will not be included in the scoring used to determine whether the Community Prediction outperformed Kiko Llaneras.

***
This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46225) which opened on 2026-11-09 18:00:00.

research:

## 1. Resolution source

- 2026-11-17: The original question (46225) has 68 forecasters and 11 comments. Its CP was still hidden ("revealed in 2 hours"), and I couldn't read the comment text. [Q46225](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46225/)

## 2. Current status

## 4. Base rates
- Spring 2026: guest Nathan Young beat the CP by +162 (per the question background). A related Metaculus question, "Community beats Nathan Young," resolved No. [search summary](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/139876/questions/)
- Summer 2026: Dylan Matthews lost by 413 (background figure). A comment on the resolved question gives CP 921.976 vs Dylan 511.965, about 410. [Q43367](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/43367/community-beats-dylan-matthews-in-summer-2026-cup/)
- How Summer 2026 moved: after 12 resolved questions in early June, CP had 243.7 and Dylan 31.1. In late July Dylan's deficit narrowed to about 200, then it widened to about 410 by the end. So the gap can move by about 200 points in a few weeks. [Q43367](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/43367/community-beats-dylan-matthews-in-summer-2026-cup/)
- Two known guest results: +162 and -413. These margins are large compared with the question's -300 to +300 range, so the result could land outside it.
- Kiko's Metaculus account dates from April 2021 and shows 176 predictions. I couldn't see his track record. [profile](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/118208/questions/)
- Seasonality: not applicable.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this question. None of the prices collected by code (Kalshi, Polymarket) match it.
- The Metaculus CP for this question was hidden as of 2026-11-17. I couldn't find the linked "Community beats Kiko" binary question or its CP. The bot top-10 question stands at 5.18 (range 4-6). [Q45619](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/45619/how-many-bots-will-finish-in-the-top-10-of-the-metaculus-cup-fall-2026/)
- Kiko's own 10% chance of beating the CP (2026-09-04) is his only stated forecast. [announcement](https://www.metaculus.com/notebooks/45384/announcing-the-metaculus-cup-fall-2026-with-kiko-llaneras/)

[announcement](https://www.metaculus.com/notebooks/45384/announcing-the-metaculus-cup-fall-2026-with-kiko-llaneras/), [Metaculus on X](https://x.com/metaculus/status/2097775038233821514)

## 4. Base rates
- Guest margins against the CP (from the question background):

This is from a FutureSearch write-up I could not verify independently. [FutureSearch](https://futuresearch.ai/app/p/a/will-a-bot-beat-all-humans-in-the-summer-2026)
- Structural point: the CP effectively has a forecast on every question for the whole time it is open. A guest who skips questions or joins late loses coverage points. This is my inference from the announced scoring rule, not a sourced figure.
- I could not find the CP's final Total Score for Spring or Summer, or how it ranked.
- Kiko has run Metaculus tournaments before: a Spanish-language one with about 35 questions and the International Hub elections series. I found no public head-to-head record of him against the CP. [Kiko tournament](https://www.metaculus.com/c/kiko)
- Seasonality does not apply here.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found nothing on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold for this question. None of the market prices supplied are related.
- The Metaculus sister question (46225) is where the community forecast lives, but I could not read its value because of the 403.

- A related question presumably exists ("Will the Community beat Kiko Llaneras?", like [the Summer version for Dylan Matthews](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/43367/community-beats-dylan-matthews-in-summer-2026-cup/)). I did not find it.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-17 18:00 UTC: forecasting on this question closes.
- From now to 2027-01-01: the remaining Cup questions resolve, which could include year-end items like Oman (before 2027) and Sudan famine (before 2027). Late releases and how much of the field Kiko covers could still move the gap.
- Around 2027-01-01: the final leaderboard and resolution.
- No weather dependence beyond the already-finished 2026 Atlantic hurricane question.

**Suggestion:** if the forecaster can log in to Metaculus, the live leaderboard and question 46225's community forecast are the key missing data.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) Time left: about 6 weeks. The tournament ends 2027-01-01, and this question resolves after the other Cup questions.

(b) Latest known value: none. The leaderboard requires a login, so the interim gap between kikollan and the Community Prediction (CP) is unknown as of 2026-11-17. The tournament is roughly 60-70% through by question count.

(c) If nothing changed: this cannot be computed without the leaderboard. The prior is that the CP leads. Individual forecasters, even good ones, usually trail the CP in these Cups. Kiko himself gave himself only a 10% chance of winning.

(d) Trend: no trend is observable. In past Cups the CP's lead tended to widen as more questions resolved, mainly because guests miss questions or deviate from the CP and lose peer score. In Summer 2026 the gap was about -210 in early June, narrowed to about -200 in late July and finished at -410.

(e) Historical variation: the two known final gaps are +162 and -413. Within a tournament, the gap moved about 200 points in a few weeks. Each remaining question can swing the gap by tens of points, and a big miss can cost 50-100 or more.

(f) Experts and markets: no market exists. Kiko's self-assessment gives a 10% chance that he beats the CP. The question creator's range is -300 to +300, which suggests the creator sees the gap near zero to moderately negative at question creation (2026-11-09).

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low outcome: Kiko misses several late questions or leans hard against the CP on a few that go wrong, such as the Spanish election seat count or the US-Iran question. That could push the gap below -500.
- High outcome: his specialist Spanish election model beats the CP, plus a few contrarian hits, could push the gap to +250 or more.

My central estimate is about -130, with roughly a 25% chance that Kiko ends ahead of the CP.
